reference_answer: Not necessarily. Mobile screens are smaller, so users scroll more to see the same content, and a mobile visitor at 70% may have seen less than a desktop visitor at 70%. Filter scroll depth by device type to compare separately, and if mobile is consistently low the likely cause is content layout rather than content quality.

evidence.title: Scroll depth tracking
evidence.text:
Scroll depth means different things depending on the device and the type of page.

**Mobile vs. desktop**

Mobile screens are smaller, so users scroll more to consume the same content. A mobile visitor reaching 70% may have seen less of the page than a desktop visitor at 70%. Filter your scroll depth data by device type (using the Devices report) to compare mobile and desktop separately. If mobile scroll depth is consistently low, the likely cause is content layout rather than content quality.

**Page type differences**

- Blog posts and long-form content: 50-70% is a reasonable baseline. Readers who find the content relevant tend to scroll deep; those who do not leave early.
- Landing pages: 30-50% is common. Most conversions happen above the fold, so low scroll depth does not necessarily mean a problem.
- Documentation pages: varies widely. Technical reference pages are often scanned rather than read, so low average scroll depth with high repeat visits is normal.

Compare scroll depth within a content category rather than across your whole site. A blog post averaging 30% scroll depth warrants attention. A pricing page at 30% probably does not.

evidence.title: Import stats using CSV files
evidence.text:
1. First you need to export your stats. Go to the Plausible site settings for the website you'd like to export the data for.

2. Go into the **Imports & Exports** section, find the **Export Data** panel and click on the **Export to CSV** button to export all the data. Note that only native data can be exported. Any data imported from external sources such as Google Analytics will be excluded from the export.

3. Then go to the site you'd like to import the data to. In the **Imports & Exports** section, find the **Import Data** panel and click on **Import from CSV** to import your CSV files.

4. Make sure to select all the CSV files that you've exported and click on the **Confirm import** button. If you don't select all the exported files, some data may be missing from your import.

5. Imported data will be displayed alongside your native Plausible data in the same Plausible dashboard. You can turn this off by opening the options menu (the **⋮** icon in the top bar, to the right of the date picker) and toggling off **Include imported data**.

question: where are the settings for excluding my own visits? I only find personal account stuff
reference_answer: Traffic exclusions are in your site settings, not account settings. Click your site name at the top left of the dashboard and choose Site Settings, or use the settings icon next to your domain on the Sites page.
key_facts: Traffic exclusions are in site settings
Open via site name > Site Settings or the Sites page icon
answer:
You can exclude your own visits by blocking your IP address in your site settings [1][2]. To do this, go to your site settings, choose IP Addresses in the Shields menu, and click Add IP Address [3]. Alternatively, if you use a VPN or your IP changes often, you can set a localStorage flag in your browser's console [1][4]. Paste this command in the console:

```html
localStorage.plausible_ignore=true
```

If you are using WordPress, the official plugin excludes logged-in admin visits by default [2][5].

```html
localStorage.plausible_ignore=true
```
Here's how to block your internal traffic from your Plausible Analytics stats dashboard.

Go into the site settings of the website you'd like to block your activity from

* Choose **IP Addresses** in the **Shields** entry in the left-hand menu

* Click on the **Add IP Address** button to add a new address to the block list
You can then set a special `localStorage` flag in your browser so you don't need to frequently block new IP addresses.

evidence.title: Let visitors opt out of being counted
evidence.text:
To keep your own visits or your team's out of your stats, block your IP addresses in your site settings. That works across all your browsers and devices at once.

If your IP address changes often or you use a VPN, you can set the same flag yourself instead. Open the **Console** tab in your browser's developer tools on your site, then paste this command and hit enter:

```html
localStorage.plausible_ignore=true
```

Do this for every domain, subdomain and browser you want to exclude. To be counted again, run:

```html
delete localStorage.plausible_ignore
```

You can also use the opt-out page above instead of the console.

Plausible automatically filters out bots, crawlers and referrer spam. You don't need to configure anything for this. See bot and spam traffic filtering for details.

By default, Plausible Analytics tracks every visitor to your website. You might not want your office traffic to be counted. Or when you're working on your site, you might not want to record your own visits and page views.

Here's how to block your internal traffic from your Plausible Analytics stats dashboard. You can block recording visitors from specific IP addresses, hostnames, countries or pages. If you're on WordPress, our official WordPress plugin can exclude views from admins and other user roles without any manual configuration.

Note:
Visits blocked by IP address, country, page or hostname are dropped before they reach your stats. They aren't stored and don't count towards your plan's monthly pageview usage.

Note: Block both IPv4 and IPv6 if your device uses both
Most modern devices and networks have both an IPv4 address (e.g. `203.0.113.5`) and an IPv6 address (e.g. `2001:db8::1`). Your browser or network proxy may send visits using either one depending on the connection.

If you block only your IPv4 address but your browser sends a request over IPv6, that visit will still be recorded. To reliably exclude your traffic, check whether your device has both address types and add each one separately.

The **block your current IP** button captures whichever address your browser is currently using. Click it, then visit a site like whatismyipaddress.com to check whether you also have a second address type, and add that manually if so.

evidence.title: Dashboard FAQ
evidence.text:
If you've just installed Plausible and aren't seeing your own visits, there are a few common reasons:

- **WordPress plugin**: Our official WordPress plugin excludes logged-in admin visits by default. If the verification tool confirms the tracking is working, you have nothing to worry about.
- **Shields**: The Shields feature lets you block visits based on IP addresses, hostnames, countries or specific pages. Check whether you have any rules that might be excluding your own visits.
- **Adblockers**: If you're using a browser extension or network-level adblocker, it may be blocking the Plausible script. Consider setting up a proxy to serve the script as a first-party connection.

For more details, see our full troubleshooting guide.

question: If I cancel my subscription and then change my mind a few weeks later, can I get my old stats back?
reference_answer: Yes, as long as you resubscribe from the Subscription section before your data is deleted. Your dashboards unlock automatically and collection resumes right away, but deleted data cannot be recovered.
key_facts: Resubscribe from the Subscription section
Historical stats are still there if you resubscribe before deletion
Deleted data cannot be recovered
answer: Yes, if you resubscribe before your data is deleted, your historical stats will still be there [1]. You can resubscribe at any time from the Subscription section of your settings [1].

citations.quote: If you resubscribe before your data is deleted, your historical stats will still be there.
You can resubscribe at any time from the **Subscription** section of your settings.

evidence.title: Cancel your subscription plan
evidence.text:
Log in to your Plausible account. In the top right menu, click your account name and open the settings.

Go to the **Subscription** section and click **Cancel plan**.

Cancel your Plausible subscription

## What happens after you cancel

**Until the end of your billing period**

Your stats keep being counted and you have full access to your dashboard.

The **Subscription** section may still say **Renews on**, but your subscription ends without renewing.

**Once the billing period ends**

Your dashboard is locked. You can still log in and access your account, team and site settings, but you cannot view your stats. You can export your collected data at any time from the site settings of any locked site.

One month after locking, Plausible stops collecting data. If you haven't removed the Plausible snippet from your site, any data it sends will be dropped automatically from that point.

**Deleting your stats**

Once you cancel and your paid period ends, we may delete your sites and stats. We'll email you before that happens so you have time to export your data or resubscribe.

You can delete individual sites at any time, before or after canceling, from your site settings. To delete your entire account or team, you'll first need to cancel any active subscription.

**Resubscribing**

You can resubscribe at any time from the **Subscription** section of your settings. Your dashboards unlock automatically and data collection resumes immediately. If you subscribe again from the same account before your paid period ends, you keep your current plan and its limits.

If you resubscribe before your data is deleted, your historical stats will still be there. Deleted data cannot be recovered, so if you're coming back, resubscribe or export your data before the deletion date in our email.

Want to switch plans instead of canceling? See Change your subscription plan.

question: I want to give a client a link that only shows traffic from one campaign and that they can't remove the filter from. Is that possible?
reference_answer: Yes. Create a shared link with the Limit to segment option, choosing a site segment. Viewers will always see data filtered by that segment and can't remove it, though they can add more filters on top of it. Only site segments, those anyone on your team can use, can be used.
key_facts: Shared links have a Limit to segment option
Viewers can't remove the segment but can add filters on top
Only site segments can be used
answer: Yes, you can create a shared link that is pre-filtered to a specific segment [1]. By enabling the "Limit to segment" option when creating the link, anyone who opens the dashboard will see data filtered by that segment only, and they will not be able to remove that filter [2].

citations.quote: Create a shared link pre-filtered to a specific segment for stakeholders who only need to see part of your data

If you enable this option, anyone who opens the dashboard using the shared link will always see data filtered by the selected segment only. Only site segments (i.e. segments that anyone on your team can use) can be used.

Viewers won't be able to remove that segment from the dashboard.

evidence.title: Share your stats with a private and secure link
evidence.text:
If you enable this option, anyone who opens the dashboard using the shared link will always see data filtered by the selected segment only. Only site segments (i.e. segments that anyone on your team can use) can be used.

Viewers won't be able to remove that segment from the dashboard. They can see which filters are included in it and they can add more filters on top of it.

This makes it possible to share only the part of your analytics that matters to a specific audience. For example, you might want to share data only for visitors from a certain country or only for traffic related to a campaign. It prevents viewers from changing the base filters and seeing data you did not intend to share.

Info:
As an example, if the selected segment contains the filters "Country is Estonia or Poland" and "Page is not /private", visitors will be able to drill down further by adding "Country is Estonia" filter. If they try to go outside of the segment, by adding the filter "Country is Italy" as an example, they will see no data.

evidence.title: Custom event tracking
evidence.text:
Note:
If you use the custom events feature, then these count towards your billable monthly pageviews.

Custom events let you measure button clicks, subscription signups or any other action you want visitors to take. There are two ways to set them up:

- **Using CSS class names**: add a class to any HTML element you want to track. No JavaScript required. This is the easiest approach for most use cases and is covered in the first section below.
- **Using JavaScript**: call the `plausible()` function directly for more advanced tracking needs such as dynamic values, conditional logic or tracking non-click interactions. See the manual JavaScript approach section.

If you're using WordPress or Google Tag Manager, you can set up custom events with our WordPress plugin or GTM template without writing code. Plausible also offers automated tracking for outbound link clicks, file downloads and form submissions straight from your site settings, pageview goals for tracking visits to specific pages and 404 error pages with a small snippet of code.

## Change your invoice email

If you want invoices sent to a different address, contact us with your current Paddle email and the new address you'd like to use. We'll update it with Paddle on your behalf.

To change your Plausible login email instead, see change your account email.
